1.overview: Paul and Timothy greet the church in Corinth and across Achaia, and Paul describes how God comforts him in suffering, delivers him from peril, and receives the Corinthians’ prayers and thanksgiving. Paul affirms his integrity, explains his changed travel plans, grounds his message in God’s faithfulness and promises in Christ, and says he stayed away to spare the Corinthians while working with them for their joy.

2.overview: Paul explains that he delays another painful visit and writes in distress out of love, then urges the Corinthians to forgive and comfort the person who has been disciplined. After leaving Troas because Titus is absent, Paul describes God’s triumphal procession and the contrasting effects of Christ’s message, which he and his companions proclaim sincerely before God.

3.overview: Paul presents the Corinthians as a letter from Christ and says his competence comes from God, who appoints him a minister of the new covenant of the Spirit. He contrasts the fading glory of Moses’ ministry with the enduring glory of the Spirit, describing the veil over hearts as removed in Christ and believers as transformed into the Lord’s image.

sections.heading: The Greater Glory of the Spirit’s Ministry
The Veil Removed and the Lord’s Glory Reflected

4.overview: Paul describes the integrity of his ministry, the blindness that veils the gospel from unbelievers, and the light of God’s glory revealed in Christ. He portrays hardship as a means by which Jesus’ life is displayed through frail ministers, and contrasts temporary affliction with the eternal glory to come.

sections.heading: Integrity and the Light of the Gospel

5.overview: Paul contrasts the mortal body with the eternal dwelling God prepares, describes confidence in the Lord and the coming judgment seat of Christ, and says he seeks to please God. He explains that Christ’s death compels his ministry, that those in Christ are a new creation, and that God entrusts him with the message of reconciliation through Christ.

sections.heading: The Heavenly Dwelling and Christ’s Judgment

6.overview: Paul urges the Corinthians not to receive God’s grace in vain, cites the present day as the time of salvation, and describes the hardships and qualities that commend his ministry. He appeals for the Corinthians to open their hearts and calls them to separate from unbelievers, grounding the appeal in their identity as God’s temple and in God’s promises to dwell among them.

7.overview: Paul calls the Corinthians to pursue holiness and affirms that he and his companions have treated no one wrongly. He recounts his distress in Macedonia, the comfort Titus brought with news of the Corinthians’ repentance after Paul’s letter, and his renewed confidence in them.

8.overview: Paul describes the Macedonian churches’ generous contribution and urges the Corinthians to complete their gift, citing Christ’s self-giving and the principle of mutual provision. He names Titus and two other brothers as the trusted delegates who will administer the offering and asks the Corinthians to demonstrate their love before the churches.

sections.heading: The Corinthians’ gift and mutual provision

9.overview: Paul explains that he sends brothers ahead to Achaia so the Corinthians are prepared with the promised gift, which has already encouraged the Macedonians. He describes generous, willing giving as producing a harvest through God’s provision and leading the saints to thank and glorify God, then gives thanks for God’s indescribable gift.

10.overview: Paul appeals to the Corinthians in Christ’s gentleness, defends his divinely given authority, and describes spiritual weapons that demolish opposition to the knowledge of God. He rejects self-commendation, claims only the work God assigned him—including bringing the gospel to Corinth—and says that the Lord, not the person who praises himself, gives approval.

11.overview: Paul urges the Corinthians to remain devoted to Christ, warns against false apostles and a different gospel, and explains why he preaches to them without charge. He adopts foolish boasting to compare his credentials and sufferings with those of his rivals, then recounts his escape from Damascus.

sections.heading: Devotion to Christ and the Gospel

12.overview: Paul recounts a man’s ascent to Paradise and explains that a thorn in his flesh keeps him from pride; the Lord’s sufficient grace leads him to boast in weakness and Christ’s power. He defends his apostleship and conduct toward the Corinthians, then expresses concern about their conflicts and unrepented sins when he visits again.

13.overview: Paul warns the Corinthians that his third visit will bring judgment on persistent sinners, defending his authority as Christ’s messenger and urging them to examine their faith. He explains that his authority serves their strengthening, then gives final instructions for unity and peace, greetings, and a blessing invoking Jesus Christ, God, and the Holy Spirit.
